questions.topic: Why the null is the default
questions.learningObjective: Explain the cost of type I error
questions.stem: If alpha is 0.05 and 100 independent nulls are true, how many false positives are expected?
questions.explanation: For a why the null is the default question like this, the governing rule is: Tests times alpha. Applying it gives "5" as the answer.

questions.learningObjective: Compute a margin of error from a CI
questions.stem: A 95% CI for a mean is 20 to 30. What is the margin of error?
questions.explanation: Applying the what a confidence interval claims rule — Half the width — yields "5". The tempting "25" fails because it names "25" where the rule requires "5".
